gloss: superficial knowledge; hastily acquired skill; slapdash preparation

definitions.gloss: superficial knowledge; hastily acquired skill; slapdash preparation
definitions.explanation: Knowledge or skills that were quickly crammed or picked up at the last minute, without genuine understanding or mastery. Implies that such preparation will not hold up under pressure.

examples.japanese: {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば}の{知識|ちしき}ではすぐにばれる。
examples.english: Superficial knowledge will be found out quickly.

examples.japanese: {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば}で{試験|しけん}に{臨|のぞ}んだが、{案|あん}の{定|じょう}{失敗|しっぱい}した。
examples.english: I went into the exam with hastily crammed knowledge, and sure enough, I failed.

examples.japanese: {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば}の{対策|たいさく}では{根本的|こんぽんてき}な{問題|もんだい}は{解決|かいけつ}できない。
examples.english: Slapdash measures cannot solve fundamental problems.

notes:
Literally means "attached tempered blade" — a cheap blade with a thin layer of hard steel welded onto it. Such blades look sharp but quickly become dull, just as hastily acquired knowledge or skills crumble under real-world use.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば}の{知識|ちしき}: superficial knowledge
- {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば}の{対策|たいさく}: hasty countermeasures
- {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば}の{勉強|べんきょう}: last-minute cramming
- {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば}では{通用|つうよう}しない: superficial skills won't cut it

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {一夜漬|いちやづ}け: overnight cramming — specifically cramming the night before an exam
- にわか{仕込|じこ}み: hastily learned — similar idea of quickly picked-up skills
- その{場|ば}しのぎ: stopgap — a temporary fix that doesn't address the root cause

ETYMOLOGY:
From swordsmithing: a {付|つ}け{焼|や}き{刃|ば} is a blade where hard steel is merely attached to the surface rather than forged properly. It cuts at first but dulls quickly — a perfect metaphor for shallow preparation.
